transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um... honestly, I'm just here because my body feels completely drained. Like, even just walking from my car to the clinic today took everything I have. It's been like that at my job, too. I'm a support worker at a clinic across town, and just sitting down and opening the EHR takes all my energy. 

And our system is so ancient anyway, it takes forever to load the charts. My supervisor, Brenda, she always gets mad if I don't log the vitals right away, but she doesn't even know how to use the computer half the time. She's always calling IT. I swear, the IT guy, Dave, practically lives on our floor now. He brought donuts last week, though—the good kind with the sprinkles from that bakery downtown. The parking downtown is a nightmare, though, kind of like your lot here. I had to park all the way in the back next to this huge yellow truck... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I just... I don't have the energy for any of it right now. Doing literally anything just takes everything out of me.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Um, I don't think so? Like, I still want to do stuff. I still like my video games and everything. Actually, I was just trying to play this new game the other night, but my controller has that terrible stick drift, you know? It keeps pulling my character to the left into walls and stuff. I tried taking it apart to clean the sensors with rubbing alcohol—because we have tons of those little alcohol prep pads at the clinic, I just grabbed a handful from the supply closet. 

Brenda is so strict about the supply closet inventory, though, she literally counts the boxes of gloves every Friday. Like anyone is trying to steal medium latex gloves. They make your hands smell weird anyway. I hate that smell, it takes like three washes with the good soap to get it off. 

But... wait. Yeah, I haven't really lost interest in my games or my hobbies or anything. I just don't have the physical energy to actually sit up and do them right now.
Do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most of the time these days?

Yeah... yeah, I do. After all that crazy energy I had just... completely dropped off, I started feeling really empty. Just hopeless, like, most days. Like I've already completely ruined my whole future in healthcare, and I'm only 18, you know? I haven't even really started. 

I was supposed to start this phlebotomy course next month at the community college. My mom was so excited, she bought me these really nice navy blue scrubs. They have all these extra pockets on the pants, which is great because I always lose my pens. I swear, the doctors at the clinic steal them. Dr. Aris took my favorite gel pen last Tuesday and just walked off with it. It was one of those erasable ones, too. They're so expensive, like five bucks for a two-pack at CVS. The CVS by my house is always out of them, though. The cashier there, he's this older guy named Frank, he said teenagers keep stealing them to draw fake tattoos. 

But... yeah. I just feel so down and empty all the time now. It's like, what's the point of even trying to go to the class if I can't even get out of bed?
Have you been feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?

Yeah, a lot. It's like... I can't stop thinking about work, even when I'm just lying there. I keep replaying every single chart I opened, every set of vitals I logged, just obsessing over it. I feel this awful guilt, like I definitely messed something up and hurt one of the patients. Even though Brenda and the other supervisors keep telling me nothing bad happened and all the records are fine. 

But I don't know, Brenda misses stuff sometimes. Like last month, she completely forgot to order the pediatric blood pressure cuffs, and we had this poor little kid come in for a sports physical. His mom was so mad we had to use the adult one and wrap it around his arm like three times. She was wearing this huge puffy coat, even though it was like seventy degrees out. I never get why people do that. My brother does that too, he wears hoodies in the dead of summer and then complains about the AC being broken in his car. His car is this beat-up Honda Civic, the muffler is so loud you can hear him coming from three streets over. 

Oh, but... yeah. I just feel so guilty all the time, like I'm a terrible worker and I've caused all this harm, even when they tell me I haven't.
Have you had episodes of feeling down or losing energy like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

I mean, I've never felt quite like this before. It's been going on for a really long time now, like... maybe nine months? Yeah, about nine months since I crashed after all that crazy energy I had. It's just been this constant feeling of being depressed and exhausted and guilty ever since. 

Nine months is a long time. That's how long it takes to have a baby. My cousin Sarah just had a baby, actually. A little girl. She named her Hazel, which I think is kind of an old lady name, but whatever. She had this huge baby shower, and they had this chocolate fountain there. It was so messy. Kids were just sticking their whole hands in it. I don't even like chocolate that much, it always makes my throat feel weird and scratchy. Kind of like when you eat too many walnuts? 

I used to love walnuts in brownies, but then I read this article about how many calories are in nuts, and it's crazy. Like, a handful of almonds is the same as a whole candy bar. Which makes no sense because almonds are supposed to be the healthy snack. The vending machine at the clinic has these little bags of almonds for like three dollars. Total rip-off. 

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, this is the first time I've felt this down and tired for this long. It's been like nine months of just... nothing.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently, like losing or gaining a lot without trying?

Yeah, I actually have lost some weight, I think. I just... I barely want food anymore. I'll skip lunch, skip dinner, and not even really notice until I realize my scrubs are hanging way looser on me. I've mostly just been drinking coffee or water. 

The coffee at the clinic is terrible, though. It's that cheap powdered stuff that comes in a giant tin, and it always tastes burnt. Dr. Aris drinks it black, which I don't understand. I have to put like four packets of sugar and those little plastic cups of creamer in it just to get it down. The creamer cups are always sticky, too. I don't know why, but they always leak in the box. We order them from this medical supply catalog, which is weird, right? Like, why is a medical supply place selling French vanilla creamer? They sell these really cheap stethoscopes in there too, the ones with the hard plastic earpieces that hurt your ears. 

My mom bought me a really nice Littmann stethoscope for graduation. It's hunter green. But I haven't even taken it out of the box yet because I've just been too tired to care. But yeah, my clothes definitely don't fit right anymore because I'm just not eating.
Have you noticed that your movements have slowed down or that you feel physically restless or agitated most of the time?

Yeah, I guess so. People at the clinic were telling me I looked like I was moving in slow motion. And I could feel it, too. Like, even just putting a blood pressure cuff back in the basket or answering a simple question from Brenda felt like it took forever. It was like moving through molasses. 

Molasses is so gross, by the way. My grandma used to make these molasses cookies when I was a kid, and they were always hard as rocks. You could probably break a window with one. She kept them in this old metal tin that used to have sewing supplies in it. I always thought I was getting a treat, but nope, just thread and needles. Or those terrible cookies. She had this huge collection of thimbles, too. Like, hundreds of them, from all over the world. Some were porcelain with little flowers painted on them, and some were just plain metal. I never understood the point of collecting something you don't even use. It just collects dust. Dusting is the worst chore. I have allergies, so every time I try to dust my room, I end up sneezing for like an hour straight. I have to take Benadryl, which just makes me even more tired. 

But um... yeah. I just felt really slowed down, like every little movement took way more effort than it should have.

These symptoms align with a diagnosis of recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe with melancholic features. No symptoms suggestive of bipolar disorder or other mood disorders were endorsed, and the episode duration and severity rule out shorter or less impairing depressive presentations.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of fatigue and low energy without clear precipitating factors raises broad differential including depressive disorders, unspecified fatigue, anxiety disorders, adjustment disorders, unspecified mental disorders, and rule out psychotic disorders with possible secondary fatigue.

The patient denies anhedonia, which makes diagnoses under F48 (e.g., F48.0 - major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified; F48.1 - dysthymia; F48.8 - other specified neurotic disorders; F48.9 - neurotic disorder, unspecified) less likely. F54 (nondependent abuse of drugs) and dementia-related codes (F03.90, F03.91) were ruled out based on the absence of relevant symptoms. Schizophrenia (F20.4) and schizoaffective disorder (F25.4) were ruled out due to lack of psychotic symptoms or mood episodes consistent with those diagnoses.

The patient endorses persistent feelings of hopelessness and emptiness, along with a loss of energy and motivation. These symptoms point toward a unipolar depressive episode, ruling out R53.81 (other fatigue) as a primary diagnosis. The depressive symptoms are present and specific enough to support continuing evaluation within the F32 and F33 categories.

This turn added F32.2 and F33.2 (moderate and recurrent moderate major depressive episodes) due to the patient endorsing feelings of guilt, hopelessness, and self-blame, along with psychomotor retardation (lack of energy). It ruled out F32.0, F33.0 (mild episodes) due to the severity of symptoms including persistent guilt, functional impairment, and suicidal ideation ("what's the point of even trying"). F32.9 and F33.9 were ruled out as symptom severity now aligns more clearly with specified depressive subtypes.

The patient reports a persistent depressive episode lasting approximately nine months without prior episodes, supporting a diagnosis of moderate or severe depressive disorder, either single or recurrent. The absence of interest loss and presence of guilt and fatigue align with these codes. Further questioning may clarify severity and recurrence.

The patient reports a single, continuous episode of major depression lasting more than nine months without any prior episodes, which supports F32.3 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, severe with melancholic features). However, the chronic nature and persistence of symptoms also keep F33.3 (Major Depressive Disorder, recurrent, severe with melancholic features) in consideration if the duration meets criteria for recurrence or chronicity.
